meta.summary: I studied the MCFC stack node from the air, feed and H2 BOG inlets (LCV-200, LCV-100, LCV-300) through the reformer, anode and cathode to the Anode Out (BV-400), Cathode Out (BV-410), Vent Out (BV-160, PSV-160) and DC-Power outlets. Deviations covered: no, less and more air flow; no and more feed flow; low steam-to-carbon ratio and contaminants in the feed; more and no H2 BOG flow; reverse flow into the inlet lines; high and low stack temperature; anode and cathode overpressure from closed outlet valves; spurious venting; external leaks; DC overload and load loss; loss of utilities; and start-up sequence errors. The main gaps are no anode-cathode differential pressure or anode pressure measurement, and no independent trips: all stack protection depends on SIC-400 in the BPCS. Other gaps are no check valves on the fuel inlets, unclear fail positions for the LCVs, no gas detection, and no start-up permissives. Most scenarios rank RI 6-12 with a target of SIL 1.
meta.criteria: Default 5x5 risk ranking (FI / SI / RI / SIL)

rows.deviation: No Flow | Air inlet to cathode
rows.causes: LCV-200 fails closed or is closed wrongly by SIC-400, or the air compressor trips
rows.consequences: No O2/CO2 reaches the cathode and the cathode loses its cooling. Cell voltage collapses and cells can reverse under load. Local overheating damages the electrolyte matrix and seals, unreacted fuel builds up, and the stack may need replacing
safeguards: VE-100 / VZA-100 low cell voltage alarm
TE-200 / TE-210 via TT-410 to SIC-400 stack temperature control
BPCS control of air flow and pressure
recommendations: Add a low-low air flow trip on FIT-110 that is independent of the BPCS and isolates fuel (LCV-100, LCV-300) and the DC load
Confirm the fail-safe position of LCV-200 on loss of signal or air

rows.deviation: Less Flow | Air inlet to cathode
rows.causes: LCV-200 partly closed or sticking, SIC-400 fault, or the air compressor or filter is degraded
rows.consequences: Too little oxidant and cooling for the cathode. Stack temperature rises, hot spots form, electrolyte evaporates and corrosion speeds up. Stack life is shortened
recommendations: Add a high-high stack temperature trip, independent of TT-410/SIC-400, that reduces load and fuel

rows.deviation: More Flow | Air inlet to cathode
rows.causes: LCV-200 fails open, or SIC-400 output fails high
rows.consequences: The stack is overcooled and the cathode temperature falls toward the carbonate freezing point. Thermal stress and partial solidification can crack the matrix, with loss of output power
recommendations: Add a low stack temperature alarm on TT-410 with the operator response defined

rows.deviation: No Flow | Feed (natural gas + water) to reformer
rows.causes: LCV-100 fails closed, or the natural gas compressor or water pump trips
rows.consequences: The anode is starved of fuel while current is still drawn. Cell voltage reverses, the Ni anode oxidises, and the electrodes are damaged permanently. The heat balance is also upset because endothermic reforming is lost
safeguards: VE-100 / VZA-100 low cell voltage alarm
IE-300 / II-300 / IR-300 current monitoring via IT-400 to SIC-400
recommendations: Add a low-low feed flow / low-low cell voltage trip that disconnects the DC load
Make sure the load is automatically reduced in proportion to available fuel flow

rows.deviation: More Flow | Feed (natural gas + water) to reformer
rows.causes: LCV-100 fails open, or SIC-400 output fails high
rows.consequences: Too much endothermic reforming cools the stack. Unconverted fuel and anode pressure increase, raising the anode-cathode differential pressure, which can lead to gas crossover and local combustion inside the stack
recommendations: Install anode-cathode differential pressure measurement with alarm and trip

rows.deviation: Part of Composition | Feed (natural gas + water) to reformer
rows.causes: Water pump failure or low water flow gives a low steam-to-carbon ratio
rows.consequences: Carbon deposits in the reformer and anode. The catalyst deactivates, flow paths block and pressure drop rises, causing performance loss and stack damage
recommendations: Measure water and natural gas flows separately, with a low steam-to-carbon ratio alarm and natural gas cut-off

rows.deviation: As well as Composition | Feed (natural gas + water) to reformer
rows.causes: Sulphur compounds or other contaminants in the natural gas, or impurities in the water
rows.consequences: The reforming catalyst and Ni anode are poisoned. Reforming drops off, the heat balance is upset, and stack performance degrades over time
recommendations: Confirm upstream desulphurisation and water treatment, and set periodic feed quality analysis

rows.deviation: More Flow | H2 BOG to anode
rows.causes: LCV-300 fails open, or a BOG surge from the cargo tanks or BOG compressor
rows.consequences: The anode overpressures and the anode-cathode differential pressure rises. H2 crosses through the matrix or seals into the cathode, causing local combustion and hot spots. H2 can leak externally, with a risk of fire or explosion in the fuel cell space
recommendations: Add a high H2 BOG flow / high anode pressure trip that closes an independent shutdown valve upstream of LCV-300
Install anode-cathode differential pressure monitoring

rows.deviation: No Flow | H2 BOG to anode
rows.causes: LCV-300 fails closed, or the BOG compressor trips
rows.consequences: Fuel to the anode falls, so cell voltage drops and part of the stack may be starved of fuel. BOG pressure also builds up in the cargo system (outside this node)
recommendations: Confirm the BOG handling alternative when the stack cannot accept BOG

rows.deviation: Reverse Flow | H2 BOG / Feed inlet lines
rows.causes: Supply pressure in the H2 BOG or feed line drops below stack pressure, for example on a compressor trip
rows.consequences: Hot reformed gas (H2, CO) flows back into the upstream lines and compressors. This can overheat equipment, mix gas into another system, and expose people to toxic CO
recommendations: Install check valves on the feed and H2 BOG inlet lines
Close LCV-100 / LCV-300 on low supply pressure

rows.deviation: More Temperature | MCFC stack
rows.causes: Air/fuel heat balance is lost, SIC-400 fails, or TE-200/TE-210 reads low and the controller acts on the false reading
rows.consequences: The stack runs above design temperature. Carbonate evaporates, corrosion speeds up, and seals and the matrix fail. The resulting H2/CO leak can ignite (fire), and CO is toxic
safeguards: TE-300 / TI-300 and TE-310 / TI-310 exhaust temperatures
recommendations: Provide a SIL 1 high-high stack temperature trip from an independent sensor that isolates fuel and disconnects the load

rows.deviation: Less Temperature | MCFC stack
rows.causes: Excess air or feed flow, a sudden load reduction, or a temperature control fault
rows.consequences: The electrolyte partly solidifies and the matrix cracks from thermal cycling. Gas crosses over on restart, and the stack is damaged permanently
recommendations: Add a low-low stack temperature alarm and a hot-standby procedure that keeps the stack above the electrolyte freezing point

rows.deviation: More Pressure | Anode outlet
rows.causes: BV-400 (fail closed) closes spuriously on loss of signal or actuator power, or the downstream line is blocked
rows.consequences: Anode pressure rises while fuel is still supplied. High differential pressure across the electrolyte forces H2/CO into the cathode, causing combustion and hot spots. Seals can fail and release H2/CO externally (fire, explosion, CO toxicity)
recommendations: Add an anode outlet pressure transmitter with a high alarm and a trip that closes LCV-100 / LCV-300
Interlock BV-400 closure with fuel isolation
Verify that PSV-160 protects the anode side and is sized for this case

rows.deviation: More Pressure | Cathode outlet
rows.causes: BV-410 (fail closed) closes spuriously, or the downstream line is blocked
rows.consequences: The cathode overpressures and the differential pressure reverses, pushing air into the anode. Mixing O2 with fuel causes local combustion, damages the stack, and can break seals
recommendations: Interlock BV-410 closure with air flow reduction (LCV-200) and stack shutdown
Add a cathode outlet pressure measurement

rows.deviation: More Flow | Vent Out (BV-160 / PSV-160)
rows.causes: BV-160 (fail open) opens spuriously on loss of signal or utility, or PSV-160 lifts or passes
rows.consequences: The stack depressurises suddenly and hot, possibly flammable gas is released at Vent Out. It may ignite at the vent outlet, and the pressure transient upsets the stack
safeguards: Vent routed to a dedicated Vent Out
recommendations: Confirm the vent outlet is in a safe location per class rules for hydrogen-fuelled ships, with a dispersion study
Add BV-160 position indication and an alarm

rows.deviation: Less Pressure | MCFC stack (external leak)
rows.causes: Wet-seal or flange leak at 650 °C, or carbonate corrosion of the stack housing or manifolds
rows.consequences: H2, CO and natural gas are released into the fuel cell space. Fire or explosion is possible, people can be exposed to toxic CO, and propulsion power may be lost
recommendations: Provide H2 and CO gas detection in the fuel cell space, interlocked to fuel isolation and ventilation
Enclose the stack with ventilation monitoring per IGF Code / class rules

rows.deviation: More Power | DC-Power output
rows.causes: Propulsion demand exceeds stack capacity, or current control fails
rows.consequences: Fuel utilisation becomes too high and parts of the anode are starved. Cell voltage falls, cells can reverse, overheating follows, and the stack degrades
safeguards: IE-300 / II-300 / IR-300 current indication and recording
recommendations: Limit current in the power converter based on available fuel flow and the low-voltage threshold
Add battery or energy storage to buffer load transients

rows.deviation: No Power | DC-Power output
rows.causes: Sudden loss of load (propulsion trip, breaker opens), or a short circuit in the DC system
rows.consequences: On open circuit the cell voltage rises and unconsumed fuel goes to Anode Out. Without the cell reaction heat the stack cools. A short circuit can cause arcing and damage to the electrical system, and propulsion is lost
recommendations: Cut fuel back automatically on load rejection
Confirm DC short-circuit protection and selectivity

rows.deviation: No Utility | Instrument air / control power to BPCS and valves
rows.causes: Loss of instrument air or UPS/control power
rows.consequences: BV-400 and BV-410 fail closed and BV-160 fails open. If LCV-100/LCV-300 do not also fail closed, fuel keeps entering a blocked-in stack, overpressuring it and venting H2 at Vent Out
safeguards: BV-160 fail open to Vent Out
recommendations: Specify LCV-100 and LCV-300 as fail-closed and review the fail position of LCV-200 for a safe shutdown
Provide a UPS for the BPCS and safety system

rows.deviation: Before Operation | Start-up sequence
rows.causes: Feed or H2 BOG is admitted before the stack is purged and heated, or before air flow is established
rows.consequences: A flammable mixture forms in the stack or vent and can explode. Feeding a cold reformer deposits carbon
recommendations: Add start-up permissives: completed inert purge, minimum stack temperature, and confirmed air flow before LCV-100 / LCV-300 can open
